sd_harkor_tower.blurb: Harkor Tower is one of the smaller formations at Palisades State Park, where Split Rock Creek has cut through a band of quartzite near Garretson in the far east of the state. The tower holds 14 climbs, mostly trad lines with a handful of top-rope routes, and the grades run from easy fourth-class and low fifth-class terrain up to 5.11, with the biggest cluster around 5.10. The stone is slick, so expect a pump on crimps and slopers rather than friction. It is a low-key local spot, quiet outside summer, when bugs and picnickers can take over.

sd_shipyard_rock.blurb: Shipyard Rock is a big granite mass in the South Seas section of the Needles of Rushmore, a short walk down the trail from the pullout on Highway 244. It carries 14 climbs, nine of them sport and five trad, running from about 5.6 to 5.11 with the bulk between 5.7 and 5.10. Several routes go two pitches, which is unusual in this district. Most lines start on the side of the rock opposite the one you meet first, so plan on walking around to the north face. It draws steady crowds, and most routes finish on top where rappelling is the usual way down.

sd_iron_horse_wall.blurb: Iron Horse Wall is a sport crag in the Blue Sky zone of Spearfish Canyon in the northern Black Hills. All 14 routes are bolted, on limestone, and the grades start around 5.9 and climb to 5.13, with most of them from 5.11 through 5.13. The style is technical: small pockets on walls that lean back slightly. A cluster of standout moderate-to-hard lines forms the heart of the wall, flanked by shorter, easier warm-ups. It sits a couple of minutes left of the main Blue Sky trail, just past a dark bulging buttress, and has open views down the canyon.

sd_can_the.blurb: The Can is a limestone sport wall inside Big Picture Gully in Spearfish Canyon, South Dakota, a gully known as a good fit for intermediate climbers. It holds 14 bolted routes. There is a single route around 5.9, a couple of 5.10s, four at 5.11, and a half dozen at 5.12, with one 5.13 on top, so the sweet spot is solidly in the 5.11 to 5.12 range. Pockets are a feature of the rock. To reach the gully's first walls you hike a trail beside a pond for roughly twenty minutes, so expect a real walk before you start climbing.
